prompt: Why can `price.py` price the two web servers before either of them exists?
hint: Look at what `terraform show -json tfplan` printed for each instance.

choices.text: The plan already carries each instance's type, and the type sets the hourly price
choices.why: Yes. `instance_type` is a plain value in the plan's JSON, and the type is what the hourly price depends on.

choices.text: Terraform asks AWS for a quote while it plans
choices.why: No plan asks for prices; the prices came from the cloud course's sheet, copied into the script.

choices.text: moto reports what each instance would have cost on the real account
choices.why: moto knows nothing about prices; it imitates the API, not the bill.

choices.text: The script reads the state file written after the apply
choices.why: It reads the saved plan, before any apply, which is the point.

prompt: In the shop's priced plan, which single resource costs the most per month?
hint: Read the last column of `price.py`'s output.

choices.text: One of the web servers, with its 20 GB disk
choices.why: Each one is 52.10 a month; something else is higher.

choices.text: The VPC, because it holds everything else
choices.why: The VPC has no line on the sheet: AWS does not charge for it by the hour.

choices.text: The public address the gateway holds
choices.why: That is 3.65 a month, the smallest priced line.

choices.text: The NAT gateway, one block in `network.tf`
choices.why: Yes: 67.89 a month, more than either server, for one block in `network.tf`.

prompt: What monthly total, in USD, did `price.py` print for the shop's first plan?
hint: The line that starts with `change per month`.

prompt: Which of these costs can no plan price, however good the price sheet? Choose all that apply.
hint: A plan knows what will exist, not how much it will be used.

choices.text: The gigabytes the NAT gateway processes
choices.why: Yes: priced per GB, and the plan has no idea how many.

choices.text: The hours of a `t3.medium` instance
choices.why: That is fixed by the plan: the type and that it runs all month.

choices.text: Data sent from the web servers to the internet
choices.why: Yes: usage, not configuration.

choices.text: A discount the company negotiated with AWS
choices.why: Yes: it belongs to the account, not to the configuration.

choices.text: The size of a declared root disk
choices.why: `volume_size = 20` is in the plan; the script priced it.

prompt: Why does the lesson show no Infracost output at all?
hint: What does Infracost ask for that the lab cannot give?

choices.text: Infracost only reads plans from Terraform Cloud
choices.why: It reads a local directory or a plan's JSON; the problem is elsewhere.

choices.text: Its pricing service is out of reach
choices.why: Right. It needs an API key and its own pricing service, and the lab has no network; an invented breakdown is what the course refuses to print.

choices.text: It refuses to price resources that moto created
choices.why: It prices code, not resources in an account; moto was never the obstacle.

choices.text: A plan with `-out` cannot be priced by anything
choices.why: `price.py` priced exactly such a plan in the previous section.

prompt: Changing `t3.medium` to `m7i.large` produced a plan of two updates in place. What did the priced version add that the plan did not show?
hint: Compare the two outputs of `bigger-price`.

choices.text: That both instances would be replaced
choices.why: The plan said updated in place, and nothing replaced; pricing does not change the action.

choices.text: That the change was 136.44 USD more a month
choices.why: Yes: one word in the diff, and a number nobody would have guessed from it.

choices.text: That `m7i.large` is not sold in `sa-east-1`
choices.why: The sheet has a `sa-east-1` price for it, 0.16065 an hour.

choices.text: That the disks would grow with the instance
choices.why: The disk stays 20 GB; only the hourly price changed.

prompt: Put the steps of a cost difference on a pull request in order.
hint: The baseline has to exist before anything is compared with it.
items: Run `infracost diff` on the pull request's branch
Post the difference as a comment on the pull request
The reviewer approves or questions the change
trap: The comment comes from the diff, and the diff needs the baseline first.

prompt: A pull request adds a NAT gateway. Infracost prices its hours but shows the per-GB line with no monthly figure. What would give that line a number?
hint: Infracost reads one more file for what a plan cannot know.

choices.text: A newer version of the AWS provider
choices.why: The provider describes resources; it says nothing about traffic.

choices.text: Applying the plan first, so the gateway exists
choices.why: Infracost prices code; an existing gateway still has not processed next month's traffic.

choices.text: A usage file with an estimate
choices.why: Yes: usage is yours to supply, as a guess written down.

choices.text: A bigger `limit_amount` in the budget
choices.why: The budget warns after spending; it feeds nothing into an estimate.

prompt: After `default_tags` was added, the plan for `aws_nat_gateway.shop` showed `tags = {}` and four new entries elsewhere. Where?
hint: One attribute is what the block says, the other what AWS will hold.

choices.text: In `tags_all`, the merge of the resource's own tags over the defaults
choices.why: Yes: the resource's own tags merged over the defaults.

choices.text: In a new `aws_default_tags` resource that the plan would create
choices.why: The plan created nothing: 0 to add.

choices.text: In `terraform.tfvars`, which the plan rewrites
choices.why: A plan never writes your files; the tfvars is where ana put the values.

choices.text: In the provider's lock file
choices.why: The lock file records provider versions and hashes, not tags.

prompt: The block inside `provider "aws"` that merges one set of tags into every resource the provider creates is called ___.
hint: Two words joined by an underscore.

prompt: Ana runs a plan with `tags` missing `CostCenter`. What happens?
hint: Where does the validation rule run?

choices.text: The plan proceeds and AWS rejects the untagged resources at apply
choices.why: AWS would accept them; the refusal is Terraform's, and it comes earlier.

choices.text: Terraform fills `CostCenter` with an empty string and warns
choices.why: Nothing fills a missing key; the rule fails.

choices.text: Planning fails with the rule's error message, naming the four keys
choices.why: Yes: `Invalid value for variable`, before Terraform asked AWS anything.

choices.text: The resources are planned with three tags
choices.why: Nothing was planned at all.

prompt: Which of these end up without the shop's four default tags? Choose all that apply.
hint: The defaults reach what this provider creates or updates through this configuration.

choices.text: A volume a colleague created with the AWS CLI
choices.why: Yes: made by hand, so nothing tagged it.

choices.text: The web servers' root disks, created before the defaults
choices.why: Yes: the update tagged the instances and left their disks as they were.

choices.text: The NAT gateway in `network.tf`
choices.why: It was in the plan of eight updates and got all four.

choices.text: A subnet this configuration creates next month
choices.why: Created by this provider, so it gets the defaults at creation.

prompt: The tagging API answered `[]` when asked for volumes, although three existed. Why?
hint: What does the tagging API answer from?

choices.text: moto does not emulate volumes
choices.why: `describe-volumes` listed all three a moment later.

choices.text: None of them had ever been tagged
choices.why: Right: it returns what is or was tagged, so the untagged are outside its world.

choices.text: Volumes belong to S3, which it does not cover
choices.why: EBS volumes are EC2 resources; the filter `ec2:volume` named them correctly.

choices.text: The filter needed the region in it
choices.why: The region comes from the environment, as in every command of the lesson.

prompt: `describe-volumes` listed three untagged volumes. Why is only one of them an orphan?
hint: Look at the state column.

choices.text: Only one was in `sa-east-1`
choices.why: All three were in the same region; the difference is what they are attached to.

choices.text: The other two are smaller than 100 GB, so they cost nothing
choices.why: They cost 3.04 a month each; size does not decide ownership.

choices.text: The `in-use` two belong to instances Terraform tracks
choices.why: Yes: they are the web servers' disks. The `available` one is attached to nothing and in no state.

choices.text: The other two were created by Bruno
choices.why: Bruno made one volume, the 100 GB one.

prompt: Match each way a resource can lose its owner to an example from the course.
hint: Lessons 6 and 7 each supplied one.

pairs.right: A preview environment after its merge

prompt: Ana finds an `available` 500 GB volume with no tags and no owner anyone remembers. What should come before deleting it?
hint: Who can say whether the data matters?

choices.text: Import it into the shop's configuration and run `terraform destroy`
choices.why: That deletes it with extra steps, and destroys the whole configuration besides.

choices.text: Find who created it, then snapshot it
choices.why: Yes: CloudTrail shows the `CreateVolume` call and who made it; a snapshot covers the case where nobody answers.

choices.text: Tag it `Owner = ana` so the budget counts it
choices.why: That makes ana the owner of something she knows nothing about; the question is still open.

choices.text: Attach it to a web server to see what is on it
choices.why: That turns a production machine into a place to inspect unknown data; ask first.

prompt: Why does the pipeline pass `expires` in, instead of the configuration computing it with `timestamp()`?
hint: What does `timestamp()` return on the next run?

choices.text: `timestamp()` is not allowed inside `default_tags`
choices.why: It is allowed; the trouble is what it does on every later plan.

choices.text: The date would change on every run, and every tag with it
choices.why: Right: every plan would want to retag everything, and the expiry would keep moving forward.

choices.text: `timestamp()` returns the time in UTC, and tags must be local
choices.why: Tags take any string; the time zone is not the problem.

choices.text: The workspace name already contains the date
choices.why: It is `pr-21`, the pull request's number.

prompt: After `terraform destroy` in pr-17, `expired.sh` still listed pr-17's instance. What did the next command show?
hint: It asked EC2 itself.

choices.text: That the destroy had failed and the instance was running
choices.why: The destroy said `2 destroyed`, and the state check agreed.

choices.text: That the instance was terminated and only still visible
choices.why: Yes: still visible for a while, costing nothing; the tagging API does not report state.

choices.text: That the instance had been moved to the default workspace
choices.why: Workspaces hold states, not instances; nothing moved.

choices.text: That its Expires tag had been removed by the destroy
choices.why: The tag was still there; that is why the search listed it.

prompt: One preview environment costs 55.75 USD a month. How much, in USD, do four of them cost if they are forgotten for two months?
hint: Environments times months times the monthly price.

prompt: Where does a preview environment usually go wrong, according to the lesson?
hint: Creating it is the part people test.

choices.text: The create job builds it in the wrong region
choices.why: The lesson's failure is at the other end of its life.

choices.text: The destroy that never runs after the merge
choices.why: Yes: a failed job, a closed pull request, a renamed branch, and it keeps running.

choices.text: Reviewers click through it and change the production database
choices.why: A preview is a copy; the lesson's problem is cost, not access.

choices.text: Two pull requests share one workspace
choices.why: Each gets its own, named after the pull request.

prompt: The 80% alert of `shop-monthly` arrives. What has the budget done to the running resources?
hint: A budget warns.

choices.text: Stopped the most expensive instance
choices.why: Nothing in `budget.tf` stops anything; acting needs a person, or an action built on purpose.

choices.text: Blocked new resources until next month
choices.why: A budget is not a cap.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right: it sent a message, hours after the spending it reports.

choices.text: Moved the shop to cheaper instance types
choices.why: Only a change to the configuration does that.

prompt: Why does the lesson show only a plan for `aws_budgets_budget`?
hint: Something in the lab, not in the configuration.

choices.text: Budgets can only be created in `us-east-1`
choices.why: The lesson's reason is moto, not the region.

choices.text: moto fails a read the provider makes after creating it, so the apply never finishes
choices.why: Yes: it answers the read of the alert's subscribers with an internal error, which the provider retries.

choices.text: A budget would cost money even in the lab
choices.why: Nothing in the lab is billed; moto is an emulator.

choices.text: The validation rule refuses the budget's tags
choices.why: The plan shows the budget with all four tags in `tags_all`.

prompt: A notification whose `notification_type` is ___ fires on the projection for the month, before actual spending reaches the limit.
hint: The other value in `budget.tf` is `ACTUAL`.

prompt: A pull request adds a second NAT gateway, in `sa-east-1c`, so each zone has its own way out. Infracost's comment shows the hours of the new gateway. What does a careful reviewer still ask?
hint: What else does a NAT gateway charge for?

choices.text: How much traffic it will process each month, which no plan contains
choices.why: Yes: the per-GB line has no figure until somebody estimates the traffic.

choices.text: Whether the subnet's CIDR block has a monthly price
choices.why: Subnets have no hourly price; the sheet has no line for them.

choices.text: Whether Infracost was run before or after `terraform apply`
choices.why: It prices code from the pull request; it ran before any apply by design.

choices.text: Whether the new gateway carries a `Name` tag
choices.why: With `default_tags` the cost tags are there anyway; `Name` is not what the bill groups by.

prompt: A team uses `default_tags` everywhere and the validation rule from the lesson. Their monthly report still shows 40 USD with no `Project`. Which explanation fits the lesson best?
hint: What do the defaults never reach?

choices.text: The validation rule checks values, so a misspelt value passed
choices.why: It checks the keys only, and a misspelt value would still carry a `Project` key.

choices.text: Resources made outside Terraform
choices.why: Yes: nothing made by hand gets a default tag. That is where an orphan search starts.

choices.text: `default_tags` stops working after the first apply
choices.why: The lesson's tags reached eight existing resources on a later apply.

choices.text: AWS removes tags from resources older than a month
choices.why: Tags stay until somebody changes them.

prompt: A preview environment's destroy job failed, and its state file is on a runner that was wiped. The resources carry `Environment = pr-30` and an `Expires` date that has passed. How can they be cleaned up?
hint: `terraform destroy` needs something that is gone.

choices.text: Run `terraform destroy` in a new workspace called `pr-30`
choices.why: A new workspace has an empty state, so destroy finds nothing to destroy.

choices.text: Wait: AWS deletes resources whose `Expires` tag has passed
choices.why: `Expires` is a convention of this team; AWS gives it no meaning.

choices.text: Lower the budget so its alert stops them
choices.why: A budget warns and stops nothing.

choices.text: Find them by tag and delete them by service
choices.why: Yes: the tags still work without the state; check each one's real state, and remember the addresses the lab's tagging API leaves out.

prompt: Which of these would the lesson's methods let ana catch before the money is spent? Choose all that apply.
hint: Before the bill means before the apply, or at least before the month.

choices.text: A pull request doubling the web servers' instance size
choices.why: Yes: a priced plan shows the difference in review.

choices.text: A configuration that leaves out `CostCenter`
choices.why: Yes: the validation rule fails the plan.

choices.text: A sudden traffic spike through the NAT gateway
choices.why: Usage is not in any plan; a forecast alert sees it, after it started.

choices.text: A volume a colleague creates by hand tomorrow
choices.why: It never passes a review; the orphan search finds it afterwards.
